cohort: 66 pregnant women with myasthenia gravis treated at a tertiary care centre in Germany
finding: Maternal and neonatal outcome in a cohort of pregnant women with MG was favorable with a low rate of myasthenic exacerbations requiring acute therapies and a low rate of TNMG and AMC/FARAD.
mod_finding: There was a slightly higher rate of operative vaginal delivery in the MG group (15% vs. 10%) which may be a potential indicator for fatiguing striated musculature in MG patients during the expulsion stage.
